summary: A report from a UCSB test group that evaluated network resources between January and March 1973, in the spirit of RFC 369. It summarizes the resources tried, makes first suggestions for concise user manuals called MINIMANs, and proposes ideas for future test groups.

eli5.summary: A group of newcomers tried out computers on the network, wrote down what was hard, and suggested short how-to guides.

subtitle: A UCSB group of novices tries out ARPANET resources and proposes concise user manuals.

tldr.problem: Newcomers to the ARPANET found it hard to learn how to use remote resources, with little help or documentation available.
tldr.mechanism: A UCSB test group investigated resources between January and March 1973 and proposes MINIMANs, concise user manuals, with outlines for two kinds of report.
tldr.outcome: The group reports mixed results, from poor to excellent, and asks the network community for comments and for documentation that might fit the MINIMAN framework.

sections.title: The Test Group
sections.content: In the spirit of RFC 369, a new test group at UCSB looked at specific network resources and tried to develop site dependent and function dependent MINIMANs (Concise User Manuals). The group was again made up of novices, so early effort went into basic procedure. Resources were checked for availability, proper usage, sample problem solutions, and access to help and documentation.
sections.eli5: A club of beginners tested network computers to see how easy they were to use.

sections.title: Resources Investigated
sections.content:
Seven projects are summarized. APL at MULTICS was used for a few trivial problems, and most effort went into finding documentation. BASIC was tried at several TENEX sites. TSO at UCLA-CCN produced interesting cost and execution time results. MIT-MATHLAB was the most successful, using MACSYMA to solve a recursive pattern recognition problem and a triple integration.

The group also wrote a first-pass local user guide for UCSB, tried to reach network graphics programs from a local IMLAC with little success because network IMLACs differ, and abandoned an attempt to learn about graphics access to organic molecule synthesis programs at Harvard when no response came.
sections.eli5: They tried math programs, games-style tools and graphics machines. Some worked well, and some could not be reached at all.

sections.title: MINIMAN Outlines and Next Steps
sections.content:
Each member wrote two kinds of report. Report 1, "Online Help for [a specific host computer]", covers connection, login and TELNET settings, help files, job status, time of day, time and money used or left, ways to reach other users, warnings, and references. Report 2, "How to Use [a specific resource]", covers access and usage, editing commands and file structures, documentation and cost, sample solutions, and appendices.

Future projects include a full evaluation of APL at MULTICS and UCSD, BASIC in depth, symbolic manipulation programs such as REDUCE, a summary of games, and application programs such as ZOG or the weather data base at CCA. The conclusion says the reports run from poor to excellent, and the group asks for information or manuals that fit the MINIMAN idea.
sections.eli5: They made two checklists for short guides: one for how to use a computer, and one for how to use a program on it.
